onchain.statement: header_start_time < header_end_time and header_end_time == inclusive upper bound of the commit transaction's short validity range

offchain.headerAssignment: demo/midgard-node/src/workers/commit-block-header/build-unsigned-tx.ts:217 destructures `inclusiveUpperBoundMs` as `blockEndTimeMs` and passes it as the header end time at line 244
offchain.conservatism: The node states its range guard over the exclusive span and the validator over the inclusive span, so the widest interval the node builds has an inclusive span of 479999 ms — one millisecond inside what the validator accepts. The mirror is strictly conservative and cannot construct a commit the chain rejects on this rule.

slotConversion.note: The off-chain half drives the real resolver with a deterministic 1000 ms slot map (unixTimeToSlot = floor(ms/1000)), so every published millisecond value is reproducible without a provider.

vector.strictlyInsideNote: Strictly between the inclusive lower and upper bounds — 479000 ms above the lower, 1000 ms below the upper. Every other published value sits AT the bound or above it, and an interval-membership rule agrees with all of those; this is the only value in the vector that an interval-membership rule accepts and the real rule rejects. It is the fixture the mutationExperiment below is measured against.
vector.farFutureOffsetNote: Ten years past the window that commits it.

aiken.selectorNamingRule: Aiken's `-m` flag is a glob over test NAMES, not module names. Every test in this family is named `state_queue_commit_end_time_*` so that the `state_queue` selector the F05 manifest gates Q60 with actually collects it.

testCompiler.rationale: Test execution must use the patched fork, never the stock v1.1.22 that compiles the blueprint. Local runs name the fork with MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN and .github/workflows/aiken-ci.yml names it with MIDGARD_FORK_AIKEN_BIN; the gate honours both, measures the resolved binary's reported version, and fails closed rather than executing this family under the wrong compiler.

boundaryClasses.claim: Moving the window's lower bound 479000 ms later leaves the same header times accepted: only the upper bound decides. On its own this case does not exclude interval membership — a membership rule accepts this fixture too — so the exclusion is carried by state_queue_commit_end_time_rejects_an_end_strictly_inside_the_commit_window and measured by mutationExperiment.

The inclusive upper bound of the longest short validity range opening at 1700000000000 — the largest end_time any such commit can carry. This bounds the accepted set from above only; an interval-membership rule accepts this fixture identically, so it does not by itself show the accepted set is a single point. That is shown by state_queue_commit_end_time_rejects_an_end_strictly_inside_the_commit_window and measured by mutationExperiment.

One millisecond above the bound is already rejected. That closes the accepted set from above but says nothing about values below the bound, so it does not on its own make the accepted set a single point; state_queue_commit_end_time_rejects_an_end_strictly_inside_the_commit_window closes it from below and mutationExperiment measures that the pair really does exclude interval membership.
The D-S12 far-future end_time, ten years past the window that commits it.

An end_time strictly inside the commit window is rejected. It satisfies lower <= end_time <= upper and is refused anyway, which is what distinguishes the anchor (equality with the upper bound) from interval membership. This is the only fixture in the family with that property, and mutationExperiment below is the measured run that proves it: under an interval-membership rule this is one of exactly two tests that fail, and all four other boundary cases still pass.

membershipExclusion.note: Those three classes were each published with a claim that the family excludes interval membership. Measured against the real compiler, none of them does: each is satisfied by lower <= end_time <= upper just as well as by equality. Their claims now name the witness selector instead of asserting the exclusion themselves, and the witness is required by name in demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-q60-commit-end-time-bound.mjs so it cannot be dropped without failing the gate.

mutationExperiment.purpose: Show by measurement, not by prose, that this family distinguishes the real rule from the nearest weaker rule that would pass the pre-remediation suite.

mutant.rationale: The rule under test is CORRECT. The mutant exists only to measure the test family's sensitivity; it was never a proposed change to the validator.

runs.note: Both failures are tests added by the Q60 audit remediation. All 21 tests that existed before it passed under the mutant, which is the defect this experiment was run to confirm and close.
Same scratch tree, same compiler, unmutated predicate.

preRemediation.method: Third arm of the same experiment: the pre-remediation test module was restored into the mutated scratch tree with `git show ae9103eb:onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/state-queue.test.ak` and the same selector re-run, so only the test file differs from the `mutant` arm above.
preRemediation.note: Measured, not inferred: on the family exactly as it landed at ae9103eb the interval-membership mutant survived completely — 21 collected, 21 passed, 0 failed. The three boundaryClasses claims asserting the family excluded membership were therefore not supported by any fixture at the time they were published. That is the defect this remediation closes.

mutationExperiment.conclusion: The interval-membership mutant is killed by the current family and was not killed by the pre-remediation family. The two arms differ only in the predicate, so the difference in outcome is attributable to the rule and not to the environment.

supportingSelectors.claim: Pins env.max_validity_range_length at 480000 so widening it fails here instead of silently redefining the maximum accepted end_time.
Sweeps four distances past the bound (+1 ms, +10 ms, +520000 ms, +10 years); none is accepted. Bounds the accepted set from above only — an interval-membership rule passes this sweep unchanged.

Sweeps three depths strictly inside the window (lower bound +1 ms, the midpoint, upper bound -1 ms); none is accepted. This is the sweep that bounds the accepted set from below, and it is the second of the two tests the interval-membership mutant kills.

Liveness control: the maximum accepted end_time lets each successor commit open exactly where its predecessor closed and re-anchor on its own window, asserted twice over consecutive windows against the real predicate, plus a pin of block_maturity_duration_v1 at 604800000 ms — the sole symbol in the merge deadline end_time + block_maturity_duration_v1, and so the only thing that can turn that finite deadline into a moving one. Three further conjuncts that compared that sum against pre-computed literals were removed by the Q60 audit remediation: with the constant pinned on the preceding line they reduced to comparisons between two closed forms and could not fail unless the pin had already failed.

membershipExclusion.note: The SDK guard is headerEndTime === BigInt(validTo - 1) (demo/midgard-sdk/src/state-queue-production.ts:92). Before the Q60 audit remediation every off-chain fixture used validTo - 1, validTo, validTo + far-future — all of which a `<=` or interval-membership guard satisfies identically, so the off-chain half had the same blind spot as the on-chain one. These two cases sit strictly below validTo - 1 and inside the interval the commit is actually built with, so only the equality guard rejects them. Both titles are required by name in demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-q60-commit-end-time-bound.mjs.

`commit_bound_header_time_is_valid` changes in any way that alters which end_time values it accepts, which invalidates the recorded mutationExperiment: its two arms were measured against the predicate as it stands and must be re-measured, not carried forward.
openParentActions: docs/fault-proofs/execution-plan.md:114 (D-S12) still describes the pre-anchor state (`checks only start_time < end_time (state-queue.ak:223); nothing anchors end_time`). GOAL_SPEC.md 5.2 requires the authoritative matrix to be updated rather than the work reimplemented. The file is outside this task's lease.

The F05 manifest's Q60 focused command `guard-focused-selector.mjs state_queue` collected 6 tests before the Q60 task, none of which exercised the commit end_time bound. It collected 21 after that task and collects 23 after the Q60 audit remediation. The manifest's own count contract should be re-pinned to the measured total of 23.

The F05 manifest's Q60 expectedNonzeroCounts enumerates four boundary classes. The audit remediation adds a fifth, strictlyInsideWindowRejection, which is the only class that distinguishes the anchor from interval membership; the manifest is outside the remediation's lease, so the parent should add it to the enumeration alongside the re-pinned total.

The Q60 audit found that the family as landed at ae9103eb did not kill an interval-membership mutant of `commit_bound_header_time_is_valid`, while three published boundaryClasses claims asserted that it excluded membership. Those claims are now bound to a measured witness. If other Goal-program evidence artifacts publish `equality, not a range` style claims, they warrant the same mutation check — the failure mode is a family whose fixtures all sit at or beyond a bound and none strictly inside it.
